title: The Iliad, Homer
subtitle: 8th century BC AD
subject: litterature
description: Not the whole Trojan War: 51 days of anger. Achilles withdraws, Patroclus dies, Hector falls. Homer shows how glory can become bestial, then human.

hero.hook: A single word opens the poem: anger. And the whole war turns upside down.

blocks.text: It is often believed that the **Iliad** recounts the entire **Trojan War**. In reality, the poem attributed to **Homer** focuses on **51 days** only, in the heart of the tenth year of the siege. The war pits a Greek coalition against the Trojan city. It was triggered by the kidnapping of Hélène. Its first theme is not Troy: it is the **anger** of **Achilles**, the best Greek warrior.

The title comes from **Ilium**, another name for Troy, a city located on the coast of present-day Türkiye. Under gods, duels and violence, Homer asks a simple question: what is glory worth when everyone dies? The poem does not celebrate war without nuance. It shows the human cost.

The mythical pretext is known: **Paris**, Trojan prince, kidnapped **Hélène**, queen of Sparta. **Agamemnon**, king of Mycenae and leader of the Greeks, leads the coalition. But the poem opens with an internal crisis. Agamemnon humiliates Achilles by taking **Briseis**, his captive. For Achilles, it is an attack on his , the public honor due to warrior merit. Without time, the hero no longer has any reason to fight. [[timē]]

blocks.caption: The dispute between Achilles and Agamemnon, starting point of the entire Iliad.

blocks.text: Achilles retires to his tent. Worse: he asks his mother **Thétis**, marine goddess, to obtain a Greek defeat from **Zeus**, king of the gods. He wants to prove that we can't do without him. His resentment comes before the survival of his companions. War first becomes a matter of ego, not just of conquest. Homer thus shows that the anger of a single man can change the destiny of an entire army.

Without their champion, the Greeks fold. The Trojans, led by Prince **Hector**, son of King Priam and hero defender of Troy, even threaten Greek ships. **Patroclus**, Achilles' closest companion, borrows his armor to scare the enemy. Achilles accepts, but forbids him from going too far and continuing to the walls of Troy.

In the Iliad, the gods also hurt each other. The warrior **Diomedes** wounds **Aphrodite**, goddess of love, in the hand. The god of war **Arès** must flee screaming. Even Olympus knows the violence of the battlefield.

Patroclus disobeys. Hector kills him, helped by **Apollo**, archer god. Achilles' anger, initially social, changes in nature. It is no longer time that pushes him: it is mourning that arms the hero. Homer shows how an emotion can become destructive.

sections.title: Achilles against Hector: glory becomes bestial

blocks.text: Achilles returns. Armed by **Hephaestus**, blacksmith god, he enters his . It's a long sequence where a hero performs superhuman feats. He kills Hector before the walls of Troy. Then he ties the body to his chariot and drags it through the dust, before the eyes of the prince's family. It is an extreme humiliation. [[Homeric Aristia]]

blocks.caption: The Trojan War on a Greek vase: glory, violence and destiny mixed together.

blocks.text: For the Greeks, refusing **funeral rites** is going beyond being human. Honoring the dead through burial is a sacred obligation. Achilles, absolute hero, almost becomes a beast. Homer shows the price of . The first word of the poem, *Mênis*, announces a quasi-cosmic theme. Achilles' anger destabilizes the world order as much as the war itself. [[Menis (anger) in Greek culture]]

sections.title: Priam in front of Achilles: humanity returns

blocks.text: The old king **Priam**, father of Hector, crosses enemy lines alone to kiss the hands that killed his son. Faced with this broken father, Achille thinks of his own father, **Peleus**, whom he will never see again. He returns the body and grants a truce for the funeral. The poem ends with Hector's funeral. , Odysseus' ploy to penetrate Troy, does not appear at all. [[Trojan Horse]]

events.title: Achilles-Agamemnon dispute
events.detail: Achilles withdraws from the fight, due to lack of time.

events.title: Death of Hector
events.detail: Achilles triumphs, then desecrates the body.

events.title: Priam and Achilles
events.detail: Common mourning brings back a little humanity.

blocks.text: The **Iliad** is not a glory manual. In **51 days**, Homer shows how anger destroys, then how two enemies recognize each other in the same pain. The poem ends with peace for the dead, not victory.
